newsitem.title: BELGIUM: G-Bank, Fortis not for sale - Suez' Mestrallet.
newsitem.headline: G-Bank, Fortis not for sale - Suez' Mestrallet.

text.p: Belgian Generale Bank and insurer Fortis AG, both indirectly owned by French Compagnie de Suez are not for sale following Suez' planned merger with French utilities group Lyonnaise des Eaux, Suez chief executive Gerard Mestrallet said on Monday.

"Financial services will continue to be an integral part of our group, but their relative weight is not the same. But you will not have me say that they are for sale," Mestrallet told Belgian daily Le Soir in an interview.

Suez and Lyonnaise on Friday announced their plan to form one merged group, of which Mestrallet will be chief executive officer. The new group will focus on four core businesses: energy, water distribution, waste management and communications.
Asked what non-strategic assets such as Generale Bank and Fortis meant for the new group, Mestrallet said: "They become supporting activities".
Suez' Belgian assets are held via its 63 percent owned Societe Generale de Belgique SA (SGB), itself believed to be a possible target for Mestrallet's restructuring drive.
"SGB is efficient and is today in a position in which its stakes will be consolidated. It sees a stabilisation of its perimeter. Which does not mean that it is fixed for always," Mestrallet said.
Mestrallet was SGB chief executive officer before going back to Paris to head Suez.
